why: Both are Reeb's theorem for a compact Hausdorff smooth manifold (universes of A at 0): a smooth f with exactly two critical points (ncard = 2), both non-degenerate, forces M ≃ₜ S^n ⊆ ℝ^{n+1}. A allows any finite-dimensional model E (n = finrank E); B uses ℝⁿ. A ⇒ B: E = ℝⁿ. B ⇒ A: move M to a slice submanifold N ⊆ ℝ^{K+1} modelled on ℝⁿ by the project's Whitney theorem exists_diffeomorph_sliceSubmanifold (V4_16), transport f along the diffeomorphism (diffeomorphism invariance of critical points and non-degeneracy from WhitneyInvariance), apply B to N and compose homeomorphisms. No mathematical difference.
overlap: B_to_A: 97 shared: Whitney embedding and diffeomorphism-invariance lemmas (hessianM_comp_symm_eq, diffeoCoord, setOf_isCriticalPointM_comp_symm), i.e. the same reduction the project's proof makes; none of the Reeb argument itself (sublevel discs, gluing)
